clue.text: Many out early to the dog's delight here in London

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a great many

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of the word early are put out of order

parts.note: a dog delights in gnawing a bone

explanation.surface: A crowd of early risers takes the dog out somewhere in London, to its great joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many out early' reads like a crowd of early risers, but it is M plus a rearranged EARLY. MARYLEBONE is a district of central London.
explanation.definitionFit: Marylebone is a district of central London, so it names a place found there.

clue.text: Intend to be stingy

definitions.meaning: to intend something is to have it in mind as a purpose
the adjective for tight-fisted, read as a state of being

explanation.surface: Someone plans to be miserly.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a purpose in mind is one sense; tight-fisted, miserly behaviour is the other.

clue.text: Someone's behind this Parliament

definitions.meaning: a person's behind is their backside or buttocks
the Long Parliament purged by Pride in 1648 was nicknamed after a leftover remnant

explanation.surface: Somebody is secretly pulling the strings of Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'behind' as 'responsible for'; it is really a backside. The Rump Parliament was what remained of the Long Parliament after Pride's Purge of 1648.
explanation.definitionFit: The buttocks are the hindquarters, and the remnant Parliament of 1648 to 1653 carried that nickname.

clue.text: British ex-servicemen recruited by France?

definitions.meaning: members of the Royal British Legion, the UK veterans' association
soldiers enlisted in the French Foreign Legion

explanation.surface: Old British soldiers are signed up by the French army.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal British Legion is the UK's charity and club for former servicemen; its members share a name with soldiers of the French Foreign Legion.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a legion are so called, whether the veterans' body in Britain or France's foreign fighting force.

clue.text: Foreshows a planetary law

definitions.meaning: to foreshow is to portend or augur what is coming
the eighteenth-century Titius-Bode rule for planetary distances from the Sun, named after Johann Bode

explanation.surface: Something predicts a law governing the planets.
explanation.walkthrough: Bode's law is an old rule of thumb giving the spacing of the planets' orbits; read with its apostrophe dropped it is a verb meaning portends.
explanation.definitionFit: To portend or augur is one sense; the astronomer Johann Bode's rule of orbital spacing is the other.

clue.text: Toil, trouble, in construction of niche — it takes an age

definitions.note: a noun here, the New Stone Age; the answer is used as its name

indicators.note: trouble suggests the letters of toil are stirred up and disturbed
a construction is something built anew, so the letters of niche are reassembled with them

explanation.surface: Building a niche is toilsome and troublesome work that takes ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' and 'in construction of' together rearrange the nine letters of TOIL and NICHE.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Stone Age, the last period of the Stone Age when farming began, carries this name.

clue.text: Murphy the southpaw

definitions.note: Murphy is an Irish slang name for a potato

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south, the first part of the word
pud is an old childish word for a paw or hand, the second part of the word

explanation.surface: A boxer called Murphy fights left-handed.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'southpaw' into south and paw: S plus PUD, a nursery word for a hand or paw. 'Murphy' is slang for a potato, from the Irish surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal names for a potato, the tuber being linked with Ireland.

clue.text: Help on 1 dn could be prodigious

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters may be made into something else

parts.note: the solution to 1 down, a word meaning intend

explanation.surface: Assistance with the clue at 1 down might turn out to be enormous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges HELP, ON and MEAN (the answer to 1 down) together.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something extraordinary, remarkable or vast in scale.

clue.text: They're handy for some tattoo artists

definitions.text: They're handy for some tattoo artists

parts.words: They're handy for some tattoo artists
parts.note: a tattoo is also a military drum display, so its artists are percussionists holding beaters in their hands

explanation.surface: Some people who ink skin find certain tools convenient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tattoo' suggests body art, but a military tattoo is a display of marching bands, whose drummers hold the beaters in their hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Drummers in a military band hold these beaters in their hands when performing.

clue.text: Prepare old fellow for final conflict

parts.note: to arm is to prepare for battle
aged means old
a don is a fellow of a college

explanation.surface: Get an elderly man ready for the last battle.
explanation.definitionFit: In Revelation it is the site of the last great battle between good and evil at the end of the world.

clue.text: Via middle route in South America

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase standing for a country on that continent

parts.note: per means by way of, like via

indicators.note: middle picks the central letter of the word route

explanation.surface: Travelling through the central path across South America.
explanation.definitionFit: A country on the Pacific coast of that continent, home of Lima and Machu Picchu.

clue.text: Concerned with big money — like "A Tale of Two Cities"?

definitions.meaning: relating to wealth invested for profit, as in free-market economics
Dickens's novel is set in two capitals, London and Paris, so whimsically it is full of capitals

explanation.surface: Dickens's novel of London and Paris is said to be about high finance.
explanation.walkthrough: Dickens's novel is set in London and Paris, both capitals, so the clue's question mark offers it as a book 'of capitals'.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to wealth and investment is the plain sense; a story of two capital cities is the playful one.

clue.text: They may be put in prison or cast out

definitions.text: They may be put in prison or cast out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown out of their places and rearranged

explanation.surface: Plotters may be jailed or banished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges PRISON, OR and CAST together; the whole clue also describes the fate of plotters.
explanation.definitionFit: Plotters against a state, as the whole clue says, risk being jailed or exiled.

clue.text: Thoroughbred horses the family, keep

parts.note: blood means family or lineage
to stock is to keep goods in supply

explanation.surface: Racehorses are kept by the family.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedigree horses bred for racing are collectively called this.

clue.text: Nora out of mind but pleasing when seen .

indicators.note: out suggests the name Nora is knocked out of shape

parts.note: mental means of the mind

explanation.surface: Nora has lost her wits but still looks good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges NORA into ORNA, followed by MENTAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorative things serve to please the eye rather than for use.

clue.text: Polish peer for PM?

parts.note: a lord is a peer of the realm
read as pole-ish, relating to the North Pole

explanation.surface: A nobleman from Poland is proposed as Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is read as pole-ish, relating to a pole, hence NORTH. Lord North was British Prime Minister during the American War of Independence.
explanation.definitionFit: Frederick North, a peer, led the British government from 1770 to 1782.

clue.text: Four sleep out — how relaxing!

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are tossed out of order

explanation.surface: Four people camp out overnight and find it restful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of FOUR and SLEEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something restful that brings calm.

clue.text: Ancient Britons are back in the Finsbury district

indicators.note: back says the whole run of letters is read from right to left

parts.note: Finsbury lies in the London postal district EC1, written with I for one

explanation.surface: Ancient tribes have returned to a part of north London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns IN plus ECI (London's EC1 postcode, with I as one) into ICENI, Boudicca's tribe in East Anglia.
explanation.definitionFit: Boudicca's tribe of East Anglia rose against Roman rule in AD 60.

clue.text: A brute, to approve a mere half-pint!

parts.note: to OK something is to approve it

indicators.note: a mere half of the word pint keeps only its front portion, the first two letters

explanation.surface: Approving a tiny half-pint drink as fit for a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-pint' suggests a small drink, but the word pint is simply cut in two. The okapi is a giraffe relative from the forests of central Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A brute is a beast or animal, and the okapi is a striped African mammal related to the giraffe.

clue.text: Child's. play to select a defender

parts.note: to pick is to select
a back is a defensive player in football

explanation.surface: Choosing a defender is easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Child's play' suggests something easy, but here it is a game of riding on someone's back. In football a back is a defender.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding on someone's shoulders is a game children enjoy.

clue.text: Like equipment designed with some relief in view

definitions.text: Like equipment designed with some relief in view

parts.words: Like equipment designed with some relief in view
parts.note: relief here is the illusion of depth in a picture, which twin-lens viewers produce

explanation.surface: Something is like gear built to give comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relief' suggests comfort, but it is depth: a twin-image viewer makes a flat picture stand out in three dimensions.
explanation.definitionFit: Such viewers combine two images into one with a sense of depth.

clue.text: Deep blue

definitions.meaning: the deep is a poetic name for the sea
the blue is another poetic name for the sea

explanation.surface: A dark shade of blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are poetic names for the open sea.

clue.text: His mate is early on board

annotationWithheld.why: His mate is early on board (4): the clue gives FOOL (Fool's mate, the quickest chess checkmate) but the answer held is POOL; no parse gives POOL
annotationWithheld.clue: His mate is early on board

clue.text: Grey has a fling

parts.note: a shy is a throw or fling

explanation.surface: A grey-haired person has a love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fling' suggests a brief affair, but here it is a throw. 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pale grey like the residue of a fire, so the colour of cinders.

clue.text: One made in a tennis court or boathouse

annotationWithheld.why: One made in a tennis court or boathouse (4): OATH is the Tennis Court Oath and also hidden in boathouse, but the only hidden-word indicator is the 'in' already inside the definition 'One made in a tennis court', so that word does two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: One made in a tennis court or boathouse

clue.text: Loves to influence the small matter of charges?

parts.note: to affect is to influence
ions are tiny particles of matter carrying electric charges

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys meddling in the minor business of fees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charges' suggests fees, but it means electric charges: ions are charged atoms.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural fond feelings or attachments, as in winning someone's heart.

clue.text: Family's without money for the baker

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the family word is wrapped round

parts.note: kin means family
L stands for pound, from Latin libra, a unit of money

explanation.surface: A family has no cash to pay the baker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means 'outside': KIN goes around L. A kiln is the oven that bakes pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: A furnace for firing pottery or bricks is what does the baking.

clue.text: Guys, say, may look on things so dispassionately

definitions.text: Guys, say, may look on things so
definitions.meaning: Guy's is a London teaching hospital, so it views things in a medical way

explanation.surface: Men may view matters coldly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guys' suggests men, but Guy's is a famous London hospital, which looks at cases in a medical manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Detached and objective, the way a doctor examines a patient; a hospital views matters this way.
